end.summary:
Practised speed = distance/time using a 100 m, 5 s example.
Calculated acceleration with a = (v − u)/t, including −5 m/s² and −2 m/s² braking examples.
Calculated average speed for a round trip as 40 km/h and displacement as zero when returning to the start.
Explained that velocity includes direction, but the distinction between constant-speed turning and acceleration remained unresolved.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: They correctly applied the acceleration formula and worked through negative acceleration for braking; the method of subtracting final and initial velocity was used correctly. They still mixed up acceleration with only increasing speed, including during constant-speed turns, and this was not corrected by the end. At home, use a simple curved-path drawing with arrows to show that changing direction changes velocity even when speed stays constant.
